title: Identification of the intrinsic strict-system clopen arrow and proper mate
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $t=\varpi_E$, and put $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For each scheme $W$ use a fixed small representative of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathscr S_W$ consist of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves $M_n$ and $(A_{n+1})_W$-linear maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$, with componentwise morphisms commuting with transitions. Use its ordinary unbounded derived category and simultaneous operations $P_u=u^*$, $R_u=Ru_*$, $P_u\dashv R_u$ with unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$, and exact open extension $j_!$ [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Let $A,B,C,D$ be separated finite-type schemes over $k=\overline{k_0}$ for a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p\ne\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $k_1:A\hookrightarrow B$ and $i:C\hookrightarrow D$ be quasi-compact open immersions and $r:A\to C$, $p_1:B\to D$ proper, with $p_1k_1=ir$. Form $B_C=B\times_D C$ with projections $b,q$ and $s=(k_1,r):A\to B_C$. Use the clopen lift of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. On systems let $\rho_s:F\to s_!P_sF$ be identity on $s(A)$ and zero on its complementary open. Let $\beta:P_{p_1}i_!\cong b_!P_q$ be the open-unit-normalized base-change isomorphism of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], and put
$$a=(b_!s_!P_sP_q\cong k_{1!}P_r)\circ(b_!\rho_sP_q)\circ\beta.$$
Use exactly the canonical open-extension and pullback composition identifications $b_!s_!\cong k_{1!}$ and $P_sP_q\cong P_r$. Under the identification of strict systems with modules over the quotient-ring diagram, the clopen projector $\pi_s$ in [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate] is $\rho_s$, and its $\beta$ is this $\beta$; hence its intrinsic system $\alpha$ is this actual $a$. More precisely the localized ordinary arrow specified by the open-unit restriction condition in [def-pur-system-tensor-mate-arrows] equals $a$. The proper-adjunction system comparison $\Gamma$ used in the system clause of [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate], and the mate of that localized ordinary arrow, both equal
$$\gamma=R_{p_1}(k_{1!}\varepsilon_r)\circ R_{p_1}(aR_r)\circ(\eta_{p_1}i_!R_r):i_!R_r\longrightarrow R_{p_1}k_{1!}.$$
These equalities use the pullback-square identification $P_{k_1}P_{p_1}\cong P_rP_i$ induced by the given $p_1k_1=ir$. They are equalities of natural transformations in the ordinary unbounded derived categories of varying-ring systems before finite evaluation or inverse limit. The square need not be cartesian; no invertibility of $\gamma$, cartesianness of inputs, or faithfulness of derived evaluation is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-system-tensor-presentation-identification] with $R=\mathcal O_E$, $t=\varpi_E$. Its comparison sends level $n\ge1$ to diagram index $n-1$ and preserves sections, transitions, open extensions, adjunction units/counits and pullback compositors. On ordinary systems the projector is $(1,0)$ on $s(A)\amalg(B_C\setminus s(A))$ in either presentation: both maps keep the section on the first component and kill it on the second. Identity and zero commute with every semilinear transition. Thus the two ordinary system transformations agree, and termwise application and localization preserve that equality. This identifies $\pi_s$ with $\rho_s$ as system maps; it does not test equality by derived evaluation.

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), open-case map; agent comparison on ringed sequence sites using the cited normalization statements.

proof.text: The strict-system clause of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] fixes $\beta^{-1}$ as the open-adjunction transpose of $P_q u_i$ followed by the inverse pullback compositor. Consequently the $\beta$ used by [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate] is exactly the stated $\beta$, with the same open units. Substitute this equality and $\pi_s=\rho_s$ into that node's definition of $\alpha$. With $k=k_1$, $p=p_1$, its final isomorphism is precisely $b_!s_!P_sP_q\cong k_{1!}P_r$, induced by $bs=k_1$ and $qs=r$. Factor by factor its composite is $a$, hence $\alpha=a$.

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), open-case map; agent comparison on ringed sequence sites using the cited normalization statements.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-ambient-exact-clopen-comparison-localization] in its semilinear-system case with $(U,V,W,Z,p)=(A,B,C,D,p_1)$. Its hypotheses require only finite type, the given proper/open square and the actual quotient system operations, all available here. Its ordinary clopen composite has restriction $1_{r^*N}$ under the canonical open units and square comparison. Written without suppressing those identifications this is $k_1^*\widetilde a_N=u_{k_1,r^*N}\circ r^*(u_{i,N}^{-1})\circ\theta_{i_!N}$, the exact restriction condition of [def-pur-system-tensor-mate-arrows]. Uniqueness in that definition identifies its ordinary arrow with $\widetilde a$. The localization theorem identifies the localized $\widetilde a$ with the derived composite $a$, including its $\beta$ and compositors. This proves the requested localized-arrow equality on the whole unbounded system category.

proof.text: Use [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting] for the sequence $C_n=A_n$ and this square. It characterizes the proper mate of the same normalized clopen $\alpha$ as the open adjunct of $\lambda_Q^{-1}$, so gives precisely the intrinsic $\Gamma$ named in the system clause of [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate]. By Steps 2--3 the two arrows whose mates are requested both equal $a$. In [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] put $L_1=P_r$, $R_1=R_r$, $L_2=P_{p_1}$, $R_2=R_{p_1}$, $G=i_!$, $H=k_{1!}$. Its component formula is exactly $R_{p_1}(k_{1!}\varepsilon_r)\circ R_{p_1}(aR_r)\circ(\eta_{p_1}i_!R_r)=\gamma$. Thus both mates and $\Gamma$ equal $\gamma$. The formula uses the same $P_{k_1}P_{p_1}\cong P_rP_i$ throughout. These are intrinsic system transformations; neither invertibility of $\gamma$ nor normalized inputs nor faithful evaluation enters.
